ambiguities.text: The specification mentions 'InvalidContractPrefix' for code starting with 0xEF but doesn't clarify if this applies to all 0xEF codes or specific patterns.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume any code starting with byte 0xEF is invalid per EIP-3541 EOF prefix reservation. This prevents accidental deployment of invalid EOF containers.

ambiguities.text: The handling of 'accounts_to_delete' from MessageCallOutput is not fully specified regarding when actual deletion occurs.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume accounts_to_delete is processed at transaction finalization, after all execution completes, consistent with EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT changes.

ambiguities.text: The specification refers to 'precompiled contract invocation' but doesn't detail the dispatch mechanism.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume precompiled contracts are detected by address range (1-9 for standard precompiles) and dispatched via a mapping in precompiled_contracts module.

implicit_assumptions.description: The bytecode execution assumes all opcodes in the instruction table are correctly implemented.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect opcode implementation could lead to consensus failures, state corruption, or security vulnerabilities.

implicit_assumptions.description: The interpreter assumes memory and stack operations are bounded and will not cause host system resource exhaustion.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Unbounded memory growth could cause denial of service via memory exhaustion on validator nodes.

implicit_assumptions.description: The MAX_CODE_SIZE and MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE limits assume these are sufficient to prevent code-size-based attacks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If limits are insufficient, attackers could deploy excessively large contracts causing storage bloat.

implicit_assumptions.description: The jump destination validation assumes JUMPDEST analysis is performed correctly before execution.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect JUMPDEST validation could allow jumping into data or invalid positions, causing undefined behavior.
